results.question: Who can get the general social security benefit when they are unemployed?
results.answer:
To get the general social security benefit while unemployed, you must meet the following criteria:
- You are 18–64 years old [S7][S8].
- You live permanently in Finland [S7][S8].
- You are registered as an unemployed jobseeker with your municipality's employment services [S5][S7][S8].
- You cannot get an earnings-related unemployment allowance, or your unemployment fund has already paid it to you for the maximum number of days [S7][S8].

Additionally, individuals staying in Finland with a temporary residence permit can get the benefit for a maximum of 400 days if they fulfill the work requirement [S1].

results.question: Is there a waiting period before I can get the general social security benefit?
results.answer:
Yes, you generally must complete a 7-working-day waiting period (omavastuuaika) before you can receive the general social security benefit [S2]. 

You must be registered as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services for at least 7 working days to fulfill this [S2]. However, you do not need to complete a new waiting period if you transition directly from earnings-related unemployment allowance to the general social security benefit [S2][S5]. If you work part-time, your waiting period is calculated by deducting your worked hours from the maximum hours in your collective agreement until they equal 7 full working days [S2].

results.question: I have no vocational qualification. Do I have to wait longer before I get the general social security benefit?
results.answer:
If you do not have a vocational qualification or a higher education degree, you must complete a qualifying period (*odotusaika*) before you can receive the general social security benefit [S1][S3]. Upper secondary school education or the matriculation examination is not considered a vocational qualification [S1][S4]. 

This qualifying period applies to jobseekers of all ages and has a maximum length of 21 weeks (about 5 months) [S1][S3][S8]. You also generally need to apply for admission to at least two study programmes if you are under 25 [S4][S8]. You do not have to complete this qualifying period if you apply for the benefit immediately after receiving earnings-related unemployment allowance for the maximum number of days [S1].

results.question: How does part-time work affect my general social security benefit?
results.answer: You can receive an adjusted general social security benefit while working part-time [S2][S5]. Your wages or salary will reduce the amount of your benefit [S5][S8]. As a basic rule, the benefit is reduced by 50 cents for every euro you earn [S8]. The income affects the benefit for the payment period in which it is paid to you, regardless of when you earned it [S1][S8].

results.question: Can income other than wages reduce my general social security benefit?
results.answer:
Yes, other income besides wages or salary can reduce your general social security benefit because it is a means-tested benefit [S1][S3]. 

Examples of such income include capital income, informal care allowances, partial early old-age pensions, compensations for family caregivers, and copyright royalties [S3]. You can receive up to EUR 311 per month of this type of income without it affecting your benefit [S4]. If your income exceeds EUR 311 per month, 50% of the amount exceeding the limit will be deducted from your benefit [S4]. However, if you participate in employment-promoting services, income that is not wages or salary will not reduce your benefit [S4].
